data.title: FutureCore Acquisition Corp. Files for IPO
data.description:
By Kelly Cloonan

FutureCore Acquisition Corp. has filed for an initial public offering.

The special-purpose acquisition company said it will sell 7.5 million units at $10 apiece, according to a filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission on Friday. Each unit will be comprised of one ordinary share and one right to receive one-fourth of an ordinary share upon the consummation of an initial business combination, as well as one redeemable warrant.

The company has also granted underwriters a 45-day option to purchase up to an additional 1.1 million units to cover over-allotments. Polaris, a division of Kingswood Capital Partners, is listed as the offering's underwriter.

The company said it will receive gross proceeds of about $77.4 million from the offering, or about $88.7 million if the over-allotment option is exercised. Both figures include proceeds from a private placement.

The Cayman Islands blank check company said it plans to acquire businesses with an enterprise value of about $180 million to $1 billion in large, underpenetrated markets.

The company intends to apply to have its units listed on the Nasdaq under the ticker FTCRU. Once the securities comprising the units begin separate trading, the company expects its shares, rights and warrants will be listed under the symbols FTCR, FTCRR and FTCRW, respectively.

Write to Kelly Cloonan at kelly.cloonan@wsj.com

data.title: Tredegar Announces Departure of Kevin Donnelly, Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary
data.description:
Tredegar Corporation (NYSE:TG) today announced that Kevin C. Donnelly, Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary, will resign from the Company, effective October 1, 2026.

“Kevin has been an exceptional legal advisor and a trusted member of Tredegar’s leadership team,” said Dr. Arijit (Bapi) DasGupta, President and Chief Executive Officer of Tredegar. “During his 16 years with the Company, including more than five and a half years as an executive officer, Kevin has brought sound judgment and a steady hand to matters affecting our Board, our business and our stakeholders. On behalf of the Board and all Tredegar employees, I thank Kevin for his many contributions and wish him the very best in the future.”

Mr. Donnelly joined Tredegar in 2010 and served as Associate General Counsel beginning in 2013. He was named Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary effective January 1, 2021, and Executive Vice President, General Counsel and Corporate Secretary effective January 1, 2025.

About Tredegar

Tredegar Corporation is an industrial manufacturer with two primary businesses: custom aluminum extrusions for the North American building & construction, automotive and specialty end-use markets and films for highly engineered surface protection applications in the global electronics industry and advanced packaging. With approximately 1,800 employees, the Company operates manufacturing facilities in North America and Asia.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Show Significant Rebound As Crude Oil Pulls Back Sharply
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - After moving sharply higher early in the session, stocks continued to turn in a strong performance throughout the trading day on Friday. The major averages all showed significant moves to the upside, regaining ground following the recent downward trend.

The major averages ended the day off their highs of the session but still firmly positive. The Dow shot up 509.19 points or 1 percent to 52,573.29, the Nasdaq jumped 251.31 points or 1 percent to 26,333.04 and the S&P 500 advanced 65.28 points or 0.9 percent to 7,656.98.

Despite the rebound on the day, the major averages all moved to the downside for the holiday-shortened week. The Dow slumped by 1.6 percent, while the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq slid by 0.8 percent and 0.7 percent, respectively.

The recovery rally on Wall Street came amid a sharp pullback by the price of crude oil, which has skyrocketed over the past few days.

After soaring by more than 12 percent since the start of the week, U.S. crude oil futures have tumbled by nearly 2 percent on the day.

Crude oil futures gave back ground after the Financial Times reported Iran and Oman will meet with Gulf states next week to discuss reopening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

The pullback by the price of crude oil also came after the International Energy Agency downwardly revised in global oil demand forecast for the year

Bargain hunting also contributed to the strength on Wall Street after the recent weakness dragged the Dow and S&P 500 down to their lowest levels in over a month.

Meanwhile, traders largely shrugged off the Labor Department's closely watched report on consumer price inflation in the month of August.

While the report showed consumer prices increased in line with economist estimates, core consumer prices rose by slightly more than expected.

The Labor Department said its consumer price index climbed by 0.4 percent in August after inching up by 0.1 percent in July.

Meanwhile, excluding sharply higher energy prices and an uptick in food prices, core consumer prices rose by 0.3 percent in August after edging up by 0.2 percent in July. Economists had expected core prices to rise by another 0.2 percent.

The data has widely solidified expectations that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates by a quarter point next week, although traders may feel a rate hike is already priced into the markets.

Sector News

Computer hardware stocks showed a substantial to the upside on the day, with the NYSE Arca Computer Hardware Index spiking by 4.5 percent.

Significant strength was also visible among networking stocks, as reflected by the 2.7 percent surge by the NYSE Arca Networking Index.

Semiconductor, retail and housing stocks also saw considerable strength, moving higher along with most of the other major sectors.

Other Markets

In overseas trading, stock markets across the Asia-Pacific region moved mostly lower during trading on Friday. Japan's Nikkei 225 Index tumbled by 1.9 percent, while China's Shanghai Composite Index slumped by 1.2 percent.

Meanwhile, the major European markets moved back to the upside on the day. While the U.K.'s FTSE 100 Index rose by 0.4 percent, the German DAX Index and the French CAC 40 Index both advanced by 0.8 percent.

In the bond market, treasuries came under pressure over the course of the session after an early rebound. Subsequently, the yield on the benchmark ten-year note, which moves opposite of its price, climbed 3.1 basis points to a nearly three-year closing high of 4.975 percent.

data.title: Optical Cable reports Q3 FY2026: Revenue $24.3M, Gross Profit $9.1M, Net Income $1.9M
data.description:
Optical Cable reported third-quarter fiscal 2026 results with consolidated net sales of $24.3 million, up 22.0% year-over-year, and gross profit of $9.1 million, a 43.9% increase versus the prior-year quarter. The company posted net income of $1.9 million, or $0.21 per share, for the quarter and reported year-to-date net sales of $62.9 million through the first nine months. Management highlighted broad-based demand across enterprise, data center and specialty markets and an increased sales backlog entering the quarter end.

Financial Highlights

  • Revenue (three months ended July 31, 2026): $24.297 million, up 22.0% from $19.917 million a year earlier.
  • Gross profit (three months ended July 31, 2026): $9.095 million; gross margin: 37.4% (prior-year quarter: 31.7%).
  • Income from operations (three months ended July 31, 2026): $2.112 million.
  • Net income (three months ended July 31, 2026): $1.858 million, or $0.21 per basic and diluted share (three months ended July 31, 2025: $0.302 million, $0.04 per share).
  • Year-to-date (nine months ended July 31, 2026): net sales $62.942 million; gross profit $22.059 million; net income $2.515 million, or $0.28 per share.

Business Highlights

  • Demand growth driven by enterprise, data center and specialty markets, with international sales rising faster than domestic in the quarter.
  • Net sales to U.S. customers increased 20.3% in the quarter; sales outside the U.S. increased 28.8% year-over-year for the quarter.
  • Sales order backlog/forward load increased to $13.5 million at July 31, 2026, up from $13.3 million at April 30, 2026 and $7.3 million at October 31, 2025, indicating strengthening near-term demand.
  • Company attributes improved gross margins to higher volumes and manufacturing operating leverage, reflecting improved operational efficiency.
  • Management emphasized continued focus on capturing domestic and international growth opportunities and delivering service across targeted market sectors.

data.title: Stellantis Talks With Canadian Workers Hit Impasse on Plan to Sell Ontario Factory, Union Says — Update
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--Stellantis is in talks to sell its idled Toronto-area factory to a local defense firm, prompting the union representing over 9,000 of the automaker's Canadian employees to declare an impasse on talks toward a new labor deal.

The potential sale is the latest development involving the Stellantis factory in Brampton, Ontario, which hasn't operated since 2024 to undergo retooling.

Stellantis last year unveiled plans to shift the production of its next-generation Jeep Compass to Illinois from Brampton amid hefty Trump administration tariffs on foreign-made cars. The decision sparked the threat of a lawsuit from the Canadian government, which had provided Stellantis with hundreds of millions for work at the plants in Brampton and Windsor, Ontario.

Unifor, which represents auto-assembly workers, said Stellantis disclosed during talks on a new collective-bargaining agreement that the company had an interested buyer of the Brampton plant in a Canadian producer of smart-armored vehicles.

A Stellantis spokeswoman confirmed the interest from Canadian defense manufacturer Roshel, a maker of armored vehicles. Stellantis added that the two sides have signed a memorandum of understanding, which signals both companies' interest in pursuing a transaction.

"The persistence of the company's proposal to close and sell the Brampton plant has hindered the bargaining process," Unifor said, adding that talks have reached an impasse and are now paused. Unifor said the current labor deal expires on Aug. 20.

The Stellantis spokeswoman said Roshel represents the best option to restoring operations at its Brampton assembly plant, "preserving the site's strategic role in Canada's advanced manufacturing sector and helping to avoid a prolonged period of inactivity." She had no further comment, citing collective-bargaining talks with Unifor.

Representatives for Roshel didn't immediately respond to a request for comment. In interviews with Canadian media this summer, the company's chief executive, Roman Shimonov, said he was interested in the idle Brampton plant as the company required more factory space to meet demand.

"We know that many automotive companies pulled out from Canada, and that's exactly where defence can substitute and bring thousands of employees back, including in Brampton," Shimonov said at the time.

A spokeswoman for Canadian Industry Minister Melanie Joly didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

Government officials have been in talks about the future of the Brampton plant. Joly has threatened to launch a lawsuit against Stellantis, for failing to follow through with the Jeep Compass production, and vowed to recover the millions of dollars that governments provided to the car maker.

Trade relations between the U.S. and Canada have deteriorated in the past three weeks after talks unexpectedly collapsed toward a new trade pact, with both sides blaming the other for raising last-minute demands. Prime Minister Mark Carney has said the negotiations with the U.S. revealed that the Trump administration wanted "to destroy our major industries, including our auto industry."

Write to Paul Vieira at paul.vieira@wsj.com

data.title: GE Vernova Stock Isn't All About Orders — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Al Root

Shares of power generation technology provider GE Vernova are a good example of the AI malaise settling over the market for financial reasons, such as peak AI spending by the hyperscalers, and social reasons, such as growing concerns about AI producing bad outcomes for humanity.

Wall Street rarely addresses the latter, but it often tackles the former. And an overemphasis on new spending has left GE Vernova stock at attractive levels, according to Jefferies analyst Julien Dumoulin-Smith.

Addressing "peak order myopia" in a Friday report, he pointed out that new building isn't all that drives GE Vernova's business.

GE Vernova's business is currently booming, with AI companies eager to secure power for their computers now and through the end of the decade. In the second quarter, equipment orders doubled year over year.

That's great, but investors will worry about everything. And fears that things were about as good as they can get hit the stock. Coming into Friday trading, Vernova shares were down more than 23% from a 52-week high of almost $1,196 reached near the end of June. Its drop corresponded with the fall in semiconductor stocks, another signal that investors are worried that AI spending has gone too far, too fast.

Peak spending might be a concern.

What GE Vernova stock doesn't reflect, however, is "peak services," says Dumoulin-Smith. Valuing GE Vernova based on 2029 and 2030 numbers missed the services opportunity. The company's service business will be half the size then that it will be in 2040.

"GE Vernova's earnings are inherently less sensitive to data center deployment fluctuations than competing portfolios exposed to inventory cycles such as low-voltage electrical equipment, energy management, and cooling," he says.

He rates shares Buy and raised his price target to $1,185 from $1,155. That values GE Vernova stock at about 45 times estimated earnings expected over the coming 12 months. Shares of electrical equipment providers Eaton and Schneider Electric are valued at closer to 30 times earnings, based on analysts' average price targets.

Dumoulin-Smith thinks the premium is warranted based on services. Large power-generating turbines need to be maintained and upgraded over time.

His peers appear to agree. Overall, 78% of analysts covering the company rate shares Buy, according to FactSet. The average Buy-rating ratio for S&P 500 stocks typically ranges from 55% to 60%. The average analyst price target for GE Vernova stock is about $1,240, higher than Dumoulin-Smith's.

The positive call might be helping. GE Vernova shares were up 3.1% in midday trading at $952.94, while the S&P 500 was up 1.1%.

Write to Al Root at allen.root@barrons.com.

data.title: 'Titanic' has a happy ending: Robust rally caps Wall Street's week of red
data.description:
Key points:
  • All three main US indexes end higher; Dow out front, up ~1%
  • Comm svcs lead S&P 500 sector gainers; just utilities and healthcare slip
  • Dollar ~flat; bitcoin, gold gain; US crude down ~2%
  • US 10-year Treasury yield rises to ~4.97%

'TITANIC' HAS A HAPPY ENDING: ROBUST RALLY CAPS WALL STREET'S WEEK OF RED

U.S. stocks rebounded on Friday, snapping a four-session losing streak as investors shook off a could-have-been-worse inflation report and girded their loins for a near-term rate hike as they searched the carnage for bargains.

They found those bargains, apparently. All three major U.S. stock indexes ended sharply higher—just about 1% each—in a broad rally.

But the rally was too little and too late to salvage the week; all three indexes ended lower than last Friday's close.

Six of the "Magnificent Seven" group of AI-related megacaps, all but Nvidia , advanced, while Alphabet's and Amazon.com's magnificence was more apparent than the remaining four.

Airlines (.SPCOMAIR), chips , housing-related , (.SPCOMHOME), and retail (.SPXRT) were among the outperformers.

All of this falls in the wake of a largely in line (but still hot) CPI report that appeared to solidify the probability that the Federal Reserve will follow the European Central Bank's example by hiking interest rates at the conclusion of next week's policy meeting.

The odds of that happening are now at 86.5%, according to CME's FedWatch tool, up from 59.4% a week ago. Even so, many analysts believe Fed Chair Warsh is more likely to hold rates steady, kicking the rate-hike can down the road a bit.

Oil took a bit of a breather on its hike into the clouds. Front month WTI and Brent crude futures settled down 2.4% and 2.8%, respectively. But both remain above $100 per barrel. For the week WTI surged about 9%.
